answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce stake before it votes or earns rewards. A randomly chosen kernel of peers verifies signed contributions and flags identities that coordinate to submit the same work; proven duplicates are slashed. On an island network partition, payouts wait until records reconcile, preventing attackers from exploiting inconsistent ledgers. Sybil attacks then require capital for every identity, and detected abuse burns that stake. A copper token helps only if it is scarce and slashing is enforceable.
